name: elbow problems overview
title: Elbow pain: sort by structure and red flags into elbow dislocation, radial head subluxation (nursemaid's elbow), ulnar collateral ligament injury, osteoarthritis of the elbow and olecranon bursitis (not scary or infected), each with presentation, assessment and treatment in order

root.title: Elbow pain: which STRUCTURE is it, and is it a RED FLAG?
lines: history: OLDCARS · acute (traumatic, inflammatory) or chronic (degenerative, overuse)
exam: LOOK · FEEL · MOVE · specific tests · don't forget the nerves

groups.title: ACUTE TRAUMA: which joint came out?
lines: elbow itself or proximal radioulnar: very different patients

head: h
Elbow dislocation
humero-ulnar joint
POSTERIOR is most common
tx: soft tissue in the way, or it will not stay reduced

head: h
Radial head subluxation
nursemaid's elbow
proximal radioulnar joint
pres: • a PULL along the arm → acute pain
• will not use it, holds it flexed
inv: imaging ONLY to rule out a fracture

head: h
Ulnar collateral ligament injury
stabilises the medial elbow
baseball pitcher
tx: • ligaments heal slowly, if at all
only for functional goals · years of physiotherapy

head: h
Osteoarthritis of the elbow
post-traumatic: earlier onset
inflammatory: rheumatology charts
pres: • stiffness, loss of range of motion

head: h
Olecranon bursitis
the most common superficial bursitis
pres: • INFECTED: skin break, redness, systemic signs
inv: X-ray if trauma · ultrasound or MRI if atypical
tx: • benign, settles once the cause stops
• ice · pad the elbow · stop leaning · anti-inflammatory

panels.title: Elbow pain by location (a fracture can be anywhere)
items: MEDIAL: medial epicondylosis (golfer's elbow) · ulnar neuritis or neuropathy · ulnar collateral ligament
POSTERIOR: olecranon bursitis · arthritis · triceps tendinopathy
